assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based therapy changed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity and show cardiovascular and renal benefit; the path from peptide biology to widely used drugs is clear, original and of very large patient impact.
assessment.attribution: Decisive work includes Drucker's proglucagon and GLP-1 biology, Holst's physiological characterisation of the active peptide, and Mojsov's identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) form; Lotte Bjerre Knudsen's drug development is also important. Three-person limit forces a choice, and the credit for Mojsov versus others has been contested.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent phase 3 and outcome trials, long clinical use and robust mechanistic understanding; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation among basic discoverers and industrial drug developers is difficult to settle within three names.
Exact priority claims on the active peptide are partly from memory and not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells with chimeric receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new cell-therapy modality; clear clinical benefit and strong conceptual originality.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain developed and clinically validated costimulated CAR designs; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified T cells. Other early CAR originators (such as Eshhar) are not in the credited list, so the configuration is not complete.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and independent confirmation over a decade; long-term outcomes and toxicity management still evolving but benefit is established.
uncertainties: Credit for the CAR concept versus the clinically successful costimulatory designs is split.
Long-term durability and extension to solid tumours remain open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Light-gated channels and their use to control defined neurons transformed experimental neuroscience and enabled causal circuit studies, including in disease models; originality and methodological impact are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Hegemann and Nagel identified and characterised channelrhodopsins; Deisseroth, with Boyden, brought them to neurons and behaviour; Bamberg and Miesenböck also contributed. A three-person prize leaves out strong contributors.
assessment.maturity: Technique is ubiquitous and well confirmed; clinical translation is early (retinal restoration), so the impact is mainly on research tools.
uncertainties: Which of Boyden, Deisseroth, Bamberg and Miesenböck should be included is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and BCR-ABL inhibitors turned CML from a fatal into a chronic disease and established the model for targeted kinase-inhibitor cancer therapy.
assessment.attribution: Lydon led the compound discovery, Druker the clinical translation and Sawyers the resistance biology and second-generation inhibitors. The three-person configuration is natural, though Janet Rowley's earlier cytogenetic work lies outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of outcome data and extensive independent confirmation; recognition is mature, and prior Lasker awards support its stature.
uncertainties: Whether the prize is judged more as drug development than as basic discovery.
Contribution of the earlier ABL/Philadelphia chromosome work is not in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical precancer and are producing population-level reductions of cervical cancer, a major preventive-medicine achievement.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed the L1 VLP approach; Frazer contributed VLP work and vaccine development in parallel. Priority between groups is a known contention, as is the role of other contributors.
assessment.maturity: Population surveillance now shows strong reductions in disease; effect on cancer incidence is increasingly documented, so timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Allocation of priority among the VLP groups is unresolved.
Overlap with the zur Hausen recognition of HPV in cervical cancer (2008 prize) may be viewed as reducing novelty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Splice-switching antisense therapy for SMA (nusinersen) offered a clear route from mechanism to a disease-altering drug for a fatal paediatric neurological disorder, and validated antisense modulation of splicing.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the SMN2 splicing mechanism and the effective oligonucleotide target; Bennett led the chemistry and development of the therapeutic. Others in the SMN gene discovery and clinical trials (such as Melki) are outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Approved in 2016 with multi-year clinical follow-up; strong confirmation, though the story is relatively recent for a prize.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer to recognise the SMN1 gene discovery or the antisense platform.
Long-term outcomes in treated patients are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that TNF blockade treats rheumatoid arthritis defined an entire class of biologic therapies for inflammatory disease and established that cytokine targeting works in humans.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini made the decisive mechanistic and clinical proof-of-concept; this is a clean two-person configuration, with antibody engineering contributions from others not in the list.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of use across rheumatology and gastroenterology with strong confirmation; already highly recognised but not yet by Nobel.
uncertainties: Relative credit to TNF cloning and antibody engineering groups is not captured.
Clinical rather than basic discovery emphasis.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-frequency deep brain stimulation transformed treatment of advanced Parkinson's disease and tremor and opened circuit-based neuromodulation; from my clinical perspective, its impact is large and concrete.
assessment.attribution: Benabid is the single credited person and the key figure for high-frequency stimulation; Mahlon DeLong's basal ganglia circuit work is a plausible co-recipient but is not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted for over 25 years with extensive randomised evidence; very mature, with some concern whether it is considered an intervention technique versus a discovery.
uncertainties: A single-laureate configuration omits DeLong's and others' circuit contributions.
Possible conflict of perception because it is in my own clinical field; I weigh it only on the common criteria.
